data.title: Bilastine
data.summary: IX Antihistaminics · Second-generation H1 antihistamine (piperidine; newer agent)
data.body:
_Oral · IX Antihistaminics_

**Class:** Second-generation H1 antihistamine (piperidine; newer agent)

## Mechanism of action
- Highly selective H1 inverse agonist; P-glycoprotein substrate, so very little reaches the brain
- Also some anti-inflammatory effects on mast-cell mediator release

## Pharmacokinetics
- Not metabolised (no CYP involvement); excreted unchanged
- Food and fruit juice greatly reduce absorption — take 1 h before or 2 h after food or juice
- Half-life about 14 h; once daily

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Chronic urticaria and allergic rhinitis
- People who need to drive or operate machinery

## Dose & formulations
- Adults and children over 12 years: 20 mg once daily on an empty stomach (updosing up to 80 mg in urticaria per guidelines)
- Children 6–11 years (over 20 kg): 10 mg daily

## Adverse effects
- Headache, drowsiness (rare), abdominal pain
- No QT effect at standard or 4 times the dose

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Drug interactions
- P-gp inhibitors (erythromycin, ketoconazole, cyclosporine, diltiazem) raise levels
- Grapefruit and other fruit juices lower absorption

## Monitoring
- None

## Pregnancy & lactation
Insufficient data — avoid; prefer loratadine or cetirizine.

## Viva points
- Not metabolised — no CYP interactions
- Take on an empty stomach
- Non-sedating; safe for drivers

## Note on sources
Bilastine is in neither book; product data and international urticaria guidelines were used.

_Sources: Not covered in Wolverton 4e or Khopkar; product information and urticaria guidelines (EAACI/GA²LEN) used. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
